messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: CDN POP iad-eu-03 reporting elevated packet loss >1% on egress links. Multiple customer backends in eu-west-1 experiencing increased 5xx and timeouts. Please acknowledge if on-call. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/23192
Sara Nguyen: acked. I see increased 5xx rates on api-prod-eu routes, spike started ~ 1765004300. Pulling edge metrics now.
Devon Patel: on it. grabbing traceroutes from our monitoring PoP -> customer edge.
Mike Lopez: adding context: NetOps email shows maintenance windows ended but no planned changes matching this timeframe.
Nisha Rao: I'm seeing origin health ok, latency at origin normal. This looks edge-side.
Sara Nguyen: confirm, origin 200s. CDN egress packet loss visible in grafana panel (iad-eu-03 -> peering ASes).
Sara Nguyen: @Devon can you run curl healthcheck from edge simulator?
Devon Patel: running: ```curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.test/health -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' --interface iad-eu-03```
Devon Patel: result: `000 5.43` (connection reset), intermittent 502/504 from the same interface.
Mike Lopez: looks like packet drops between PoP and transit partner. Running mtr now.
Devon Patel: mtr shows packet loss starting after our egress router, consistent across multiple transit peers.
Sara Nguyen: escalated to NetOps (Kevin) via DM, tagging here to coordinate routing work. @Kevin O'Leary
Kevin O'Leary: joining. seeing BGP flaps from one of the IX peers servicing iad-eu-03, probable link degradation. Not seeing config changes on our side.
Nisha Rao: quick customer impact check: list of active customers routed through iad-eu-03 -- table shows 12 critical customers with traffic weighting ~18% of eu-west-1 requests.
Sara Nguyen: initial severity: P2 -> potential P1 if persists. We need mitigation: options are BGP withdraw/traffic shift to iad-eu-02, or DNS failover to alternate POPs. Thoughts?
Devon Patel: BGP withdraw on the affected clients' prefixes will force alternate PoPs. Can do targeted community-tag withdraw for specific transit peers. Faster than DNS TTL change.
Mike Lopez: Agree. We should also prep DNS low-TTL failover as backup. Lowering TTL to 30s for the CNAMEs will help if we need to flip later.
Kevin O'Leary: I'll coordinate BGP actions with transit. Plan: 1) apply no-export community for iad-eu-03 announced prefixes to the affected peers 2) monitor packet loss and 5xx 3) revert when stable.
Sara Nguyen: timeline?
Kevin O'Leary: pushing now. ETA 1-2 min for routes to converge.
Sara Nguyen: :eyes: watching graphs.
Devon Patel: running synthetic checks every 15s.
pagerduty-bot: Devon Patel acknowledged the incident.
Mike Lopez: after BGP change, initial convergence shows lower packet loss on egress, 5xx down by ~60%.
Sara Nguyen: :white_check_mark: looks better from our end — still seeing a few customers with elevated errors, likely due to session affinity to failing PoP.
Nisha Rao: building list of affected customers for comms: Customer A (payments), Customer D (chat), Customer F (search). Severity notes attached.
Devon Patel: triggering targeted cache rehydrates on fallback PoP to warm sessions. Command: ```admin reroute --from iad-eu-03 --to iad-eu-02 --customers "A,D,F"```
Sara Nguyen: doing a quick check with downstream partners, @Mike can you confirm transit reported link flapping resolved?
Mike Lopez: transit confirms a degraded fiber pair at their edge, they moved circuits to backup. We should leave BGP withdraw in place for a few more minutes to ensure stable paths.
Kevin O'Leary: agreed. Holding for 10 more minutes. I'll post when I plan to re-advertise.
Devon Patel: note: latency on alternative path is +22ms for some regions, but within SLO for API. Monitoring for error rate regression.
Sara Nguyen: Customer impact assessment: 12 critical customers, most had increased 5xx rates for 8–12 min. Payment customers saw retries succeed; no confirmed revenue loss yet but higher error rate for short window. We'll draft a summary for post-incident.
Nisha Rao: prepping customer-facing status update draft: short, transparent, note impacted region, mitigation actions (traffic shifted, partner fixed fiber), ETA for full restoration.
Sara Nguyen: handoff: I'm approaching end of shift, Devon will be primary on-call after 1765004600. Devon, anything you need from me before handoff?
Devon Patel: go-ahead: keep BGP withdraw until full steady state and all 5xx <0.1%. I'll own until 1765007000. Please escalate to P1 if customer outages re-escalate.
Sara Nguyen: copying postmortem owners: @Nisha, @Kevin. I'll update the incident channel with timeline after this. Thanks all. :pray:
pagerduty-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by Devon Patel.
Devon Patel: marking mitigated after sustained reduction. Still monitoring for residual errors.
Mike Lopez: running final verification sweep across PoPs and transit peers — all green.
Nisha Rao: collecting logs and customer error samples for RCA appendix.
Kevin O'Leary: I'll coordinate with transit on root cause note (fiber pair fault + transient BGP instability). Will request CIR ticket and timeline.
Sara Nguyen: final note: lower TTL prep helped but BGP withdraw was primary fix. Post-incident actions: 1) improve early detection for PoP egress packet loss 2) automate targeted community withdraw playbook 3) update runbook with decision tree (BGP vs DNS).
Devon Patel: handing over—I'll update the incident channel if anything changes.
Sara Nguyen: thanks team, good work. :tada:
Devon Patel: :thumbsup:
